title: Rafael and the Autopsy
premise: Retired detective Jonah Nystrom, now barely keeping afloat running a dusty bookshop, is handed the personal effects of a missing woman, Elise Varga, by her estranged daughter. Inside her diary, entries continue for three weeks after the date she vanished — written in a hand that isn't quite hers. As Jonah decodes a ledger of payments hidden in the bookshop's own inventory records, they discover Elise was laundering money for someone inside the police department she once trusted, and that her 'disappearance' was staged to protect a witness who can expose a decades-old cover-up. The trail ends at the county morgue, where an unclaimed body labeled with a false name waits under case number 4471; the autopsy report, if Jonah can get it unsealed before it's destroyed, proves Elise faked nothing — she's dead, and someone very close to her signed off on the lie. In the end, Jonah must choose between protecting the found family of misfits who've gathered around the bookshop and publishing the truth that will burn down everything Elise died to shield.
about_author: Casper Fairweather is the pen name of a former small-town coroner's assistant who spent eleven years filing death certificates before turning to fiction. They write mysteries from a converted funeral parlor on the coast of Maine, where the fog does half the atmospheric work.

chapters.title: The Customer Who Never Buys
chapters.summary: Jonah Nystrom's POV. A rainy Tuesday at Nystrom & Daughters Books, where there are no daughters and rent is overdue. Mara Varga arrives asking if her missing mother ever sold books here. Jonah recognizes the name from an old case file. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity rekindling a dormant instinct.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Mara leaves her mother's diary as collateral for a loan Jonah doesn't want to give. Reading it that night, Jonah finds dated entries continuing three weeks past Elise's disappearance — the handwriting subtly wrong, the content mundane but precise. Emotional beat: cold dread dressed as professional interest.

chapters.title: Shelf 12, Row C
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cross-referencing diary references against the shop's old inventory ledger, Jonah finds purchase orders that don't match any real supplier — coded payments routed through the bookshop years ago, when it belonged to Elise's late husband. Emotional beat: the shop itself becomes untrustworthy ground.

chapters.title: What Mara Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara admits she and Elise hadn't spoken in six years after a fight over Mara's ex-husband, a county clerk. She came not for closure but because Elise mailed her a postcard dated after the disappearance. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Old Partner Problem
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah visits retired forensics tech Deshawn Cole, the closest thing to family they have, who warns them off: the original missing-persons file was closed fast, too fast, and the detective who closed it still works county homicide. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling one way, truth the other.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Decoding the cipher — prices keyed to hymnal page numbers — Jonah maps payments to dates matching sealed court cases, including one involving a death in custody twenty-two years ago. Emotional beat: vertigo at the scale of what Elise was entangled in.

chapters.title: Someone Rearranged the Stock
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah returns to find the shop searched, the diary's hiding place disturbed but the book left behind — a message. Detective Ilsa Brandt visits, friendly and wrong, asking routine questions about Mara. Emotional beat: hunted without proof of the hunter.

chapters.title: The Witness Nobody Buried
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara tracks down Ruth Okonkwo, the widow of the man who died in custody, who reveals Elise visited her every month for two decades, leaving cash and apologies. Emotional beat: Elise transforms from stranger to penitent.

chapters.title: Case Number 4471
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Following a diary reference to 'the quiet room,' Jonah pulls morgue intake records and finds an unclaimed body logged the week after Elise vanished, released for cremation in nine days. Emotional beat: a clock starting to tick audibly.

chapters.title: Dinner with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Deshawn's POV. Deshawn hosts his monthly dinner for Jonah and the shop's orbit of strays — teen employee Priya, insomniac regular Mr. Anand — and watches Jonah fail to enjoy it, distracted by the countdown. Emotional beat: found family as both refuge and stake.

chapters.title: Brandt's Version
chapters.summary: Ilsa Brandt's POV. Brandt confronts Jonah privately, revealing she knows about the ledger — and claims she's been investigating the cover-up from inside for years, and that Elise was her informant. Emotional beat: an alliance offered by someone who may be the killer.

chapters.title: The Postmark Lie
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah proves the postcard to Mara was mailed from within the county, postmarked after Elise's car was found burned — meaning someone alive sent it. The handwriting matches the diary's later entries. Emotional beat: hope curdling into manipulation.

chapters.title: Priya Reads Everything
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Teen bookseller Priya, who has been quietly shelving Jonah's scattered notes, spots the pattern they missed: the coded payments stop the week of the custody death anniversary each year. She also noticed a man photographing the shop. Emotional beat: the kid becomes essential.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Quiet Room
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah and Deshawn access the morgue's cold storage after hours using Deshawn's lapsed credentials. Body 4471's chart lists dental records 'pending' for twenty years — deliberately never matched. Emotional beat: sacrilege and certainty in equal measure.

chapters.title: Not Her Body
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The remains are male. Elise never died here — so either she's alive, or her body is somewhere no one ever looked. Jonah realizes the diary's final entry describes a place: the flooded quarry behind the old fairgrounds. Emotional beat: grief arriving before confirmation.

chapters.title: The Quarry
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara and Jonah search the quarry at dawn and find what the water gave back decades late: nothing of Elise, but her husband's old tackle box containing the original ledger pages and a confession letter naming the officer who killed Ruth Okonkwo's husband. Emotional beat: the truth physically heavy in their hands.

chapters.title: The Confession Letter
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The letter reveals Elise's husband witnessed the killing, was coerced into silence, laundered hush money until his own convenient death — and Elise spent her life gathering evidence, planning to go public before she disappeared. Emotional beat: understanding the cost of loyalty to the guilty.

chapters.title: Trap at the Shop
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The photographer returns; Priya triggers the alarm and hides Mr. Anand in the stockroom while Brandt arrives — and arrests the photographer, a retired deputy, in front of witnesses. But Brandt then asks Jonah to hand over the letter 'for safekeeping.' Emotional beat: trust balanced on a knife edge.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah tests Brandt with a fabricated detail only the killer would correct — and she does. Confronted, Brandt breaks: she wasn't Elise's ally but the daughter of the implicated officer, protecting him, and she was in the quarry the night Elise fell. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Autopsy
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Climax. With Deshawn and a state investigator Brandt didn't know was already probing the department, Jonah forces the exhumation and review of case 4471 and the quarry evidence. Brandt confesses on record; the cover-up unravels publicly. Emotional beat: truth winning at last, at full price.

chapters.title: What We Bury, What We Keep
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Elise's memorial at the bookshop — Mara reads the diary's true final entry, addressed to her, forgiving them both. Ruth Okonkwo attends. The found family fills the folding chairs. Emotional beat: mourning braided with belonging.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Weeks later, the shop survives on new foot traffic drawn by the case; Jonah shelves a copy of the published story and turns the sign to OPEN. A customer asks if the owner really solved it. 'The owner just refused to stop reading,' Jonah says. Emotional beat: quiet peace earned, door left open.
